title: OS command execution via {sink} ({lang}) — review required
description: The {lang} sink {sink} launches processes. Untrusted input in the command becomes command injection. This lexical rule flags the sink; the reviewer confirms arguments are trusted or passed as vectors via {safe}.
remediation: Use {safe} with separate arguments, never interpolated command strings.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: any {sink} call matches. Other languages' launchers are separate rules.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on the {sink} call in {lang} code.
fp: Fixed maintenance commands are the common false positive.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} executes external commands. Shell metacharacters in untrusted input break out of the intended command. The remedy is {safe}.
applicability: {lang} codebases launching processes; single-line lexical scope.
risk: Command execution on untrusted input; HIGH severity.
why: {sink} launches {lang} processes from strings, so untrusted input becomes command injection.
fix: Allowlist commands where a shell is unavoidable.
Re-run the scan and confirm no sink remains on untrusted input.
verifyT: Rescan shows no sink on untrusted input.

title: Dynamic evaluation via {sink} ({lang}) — review required
description: The {lang} sink {sink} runs strings as code. Untrusted input becomes code execution. This lexical rule flags the sink; the reviewer confirms trust or replaces it with {safe}.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: any {sink} call matches.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on the {sink} call in {lang} code.
fp: Trusted tooling is the common false positive.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} runs a string as code, so any value that reaches the string executes with the process's privileges. The remedy is a fixed code path ({safe}) instead of runtime evaluation.
applicability: {lang} codebases evaluating strings; single-line lexical scope.
risk: Code execution on untrusted input; HIGH severity.
fix: Re-run the scan and confirm no sink remains on untrusted input.
verifyT: Rescan shows no sink on untrusted input.

limitation: Lexical, line-based: matches variable evaluation.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on variable evaluation in {lang} code.
fp: Trusted macro expansion is the common false positive.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} evaluates variable content as code. The remedy is {safe}.
risk: Code execution on untrusted input; HIGH severity.
fix: Re-run the scan and confirm none remains.

title: Unsafe unarchiving via {sink} ({lang}) — review required
description: The {lang} call {sink} rebuilds objects from archive bytes. Hostile archives instantiate unexpected classes. This lexical rule flags the call; the reviewer confirms trust or requires {safe}.
remediation: Require secure coding ({safe}) and allowlist classes.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: any {sink} call matches.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on the {sink} call in {lang} code.
fp: Trusted local archives are the common false positive.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} decodes archived objects. The remedy is {safe}.
applicability: {lang} codebases decoding archives; single-line lexical scope.
fix: Use {safe} with an allowlisted class set.
Re-run the scan and confirm no raw call remains on untrusted bytes.
verifyT: Rescan shows no raw call on untrusted bytes.

title: MD5 use via {sink} ({lang}) — review required
description: The {lang} call {sink} computes MD5, broken for security uses. This lexical rule flags the call; the reviewer confirms a checksum use or switches to {safe}.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: matches any {sink} call.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on the {sink} call in {lang} code.
fp: Checksums are the common false positive.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} computes MD5, whose collisions are cheap to construct, so integrity or identity checks built on it can be defeated. The remedy is a modern digest ({safe}) for security purposes.
applicability: {lang} codebases hashing with {sink}; single-line lexical scope.
risk: Forged digests where security is assumed; LOW severity.
fix: Justify remaining checksum uses in comments.

title: MD5 package use ({lang}) — review required
description: Code in {lang} uses the MD5 package: {sink}. MD5 is broken for security uses. This lexical rule flags the use; the reviewer confirms a checksum or migrates.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: matches the package name.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on MD5 use in {lang} code.
fp: Checksums are the common false positive.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} names MD5 hashing, so any protection derived from it inherits the same collision weakness. The remedy is to migrate the security use to {safe}; checksums against accidental corruption can stay.
verifyT: Rescan shows no unjustified MD5 use.

title: SHA-1 package use ({lang}) — review required
description: Code in {lang} uses the SHA-1 package: {sink}. SHA-1 is deprecated for security uses. This lexical rule flags the use; the reviewer confirms interop or migrates.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: matches the package name.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on SHA-1 use in {lang} code.
fp: Interop is the common false positive.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} names SHA-1 hashing, which is deprecated because chosen-prefix collisions are practical. The remedy is to move signature and identity uses to {safe}.
verifyT: Rescan shows no unjustified SHA-1 use.

title: Predictable randomness via {sink} ({lang}) — review required
description: The {lang} call {sink} draws predictable values. Security uses need {safe}. This lexical rule flags the call; the reviewer confirms a statistical use.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: matches any {sink} call.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on the {sink} call in {lang} code.
fp: Simulations are the common false positive.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} draws predictable values from a general-purpose generator, so tokens, nonces or identifiers built from it can be guessed. Security uses need a cryptographic source ({safe}).
verifyT: Rescan shows no {sink} feeding security values.

title: Unescaped template output ({fw}, {lang}) — review required
description: A {fw} template outputs a value unescaped: {sink}. Untrusted input becomes script in victims' browsers. This lexical rule flags the construct; the reviewer confirms trust or switches to {safe}.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: matches the construct regardless of value trust.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on unescaped output in {fw} templates.
fp: Trusted constant markup is the common false positive.
recordDesc: In {fw}, {sink} bypasses the template engine's autoescaping, so a value containing markup is written into the page as HTML. The remedy is the escaped form ({safe}) unless the value is a trusted constant.
fix: Sanitize values that must stay raw.
verifyT: Rescan shows no unescaped output on untrusted values.

title: SQL built by concatenation ({lang}) — review required
description: A {lang} query assembles SQL from parts: {sink}. Untrusted parts rewrite the statement. This lexical rule flags the assembly; the reviewer confirms trust or parameterizes via {safe}.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: any assembled query matches.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on assembled SQL in {lang} code.
fp: Fixed fragments are the common false positive.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} mixes SQL text with values. The remedy is {safe}.
verifyT: Rescan shows no assembled query on untrusted input.

title: Server-side fetch of assembled URL ({lang}) — review required
description: A {lang} client fetches an assembled URL: {sink}. Untrusted parts reach internal hosts. This lexical rule flags the fetch; the reviewer confirms the host is fixed or allowlisted via {safe}.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: any assembled fetch URL matches.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on assembled fetch URLs in {lang} code.
fp: Fixed hosts are the common false positive.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} fetches a URL composed from runtime input, so a caller can redirect the request to internal hosts or cloud metadata. The remedy is a fixed destination or an allowlist ({safe}).
risk: Internal access via metadata and intranet; HIGH severity.

title: Sensitive value in log call ({lang}) — review required
description: A {lang} log call outputs a credential-named value: {sink}. Logs persist and spread. This lexical rule flags the call; the reviewer confirms non-sensitivity or redacts.
remediation: Log {safe} instead and scrub historic logs.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: matches credential-adjacent names.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on credential-named log values in {lang} code.
fp: Presence flags are the common false positive.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} logs a credential-named value. The remedy is {safe}.
risk: Credential disclosure via logs; MEDIUM severity.
verifyT: Rescan shows no credential-named log values.

title: File access built from input ({lang}) — review required
description: A {lang} file operation builds its path from input: {sink}. Traversal sequences escape the directory. This lexical rule flags the construction; the reviewer confirms confinement via {safe}.
remediation: Confine with {safe} or map input through an allowlist.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: any input-built path matches.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on input-built paths in {lang} code.
fp: Trusted directories are the common false positive.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} builds a file path from input, so traversal sequences can step outside the intended directory. The remedy is confinement to a base directory ({safe}) plus normalization and an allowlist.
risk: Arbitrary file read or write; HIGH severity.
verifyT: Rescan shows no open path; traversal probes rejected.

title: TLS verification disabled ({lang}) — review required
description: TLS verification is switched off in {lang}: {sink}. Any certificate is then trusted. This lexical rule flags the switch; the reviewer restores {safe}.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: matches the switch regardless of environment.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on TLS-disabling settings in {lang} code.
fp: Test fixtures are the common false positive.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} disables TLS authenticity. The remedy is {safe}.
verifyT: Rescan shows no disabling switch outside tests.

title: Redirect via {sink} ({lang}) — review required
description: The {lang} call {sink} redirects to a computed address. Untrusted input enables phishing. This lexical rule flags the call; the reviewer validates targets via {safe}.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: any {sink} call matches.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on the {sink} call in {lang} code.
fp: Fixed targets are the common false positive.
recordDesc: In {lang}, {sink} redirects to an address taken from input, so the trusted domain can be used to make phishing links look legitimate. The remedy is validation against known destinations ({safe}).

title: Framework SQL built from input ({fw}) — review required
description: A {fw} data call assembles SQL: {sink}. Interpolated values rewrite the statement. This lexical rule flags the assembly; the reviewer parameterizes via {safe}.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: any assembled query matches.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on assembled SQL ({fw}).
fp: Fixed fragments are the common false positive.
recordDesc: In {fw}, {sink} mixes SQL with values. The remedy is {safe}.
verifyT: Rescan shows no assembled query on untrusted input.

title: Weak service hardening ({fw}) — review required
description: {fw} weakens a hardening control: {sink}. Each relaxation widens local or network impact. This lexical rule flags the setting; the reviewer restores {safe}.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: matches the setting regardless of host trust.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on weak settings ({fw}).
fp: Lab hosts are the common false positive.
recordDesc: For {fw}, {sink} relaxes a hardening control, so a local or network actor gains access the default configuration would refuse. The remedy is to restore the strict setting ({safe}) and review why it was loosened.

haproxy:stats: no stats socket or strict level

systemd:notmp.recordDesc: PrivateTmp=no removes the private /tmp and /var/tmp namespace of the unit, so the service shares temp paths with every local user.
systemd:notmp.risk: Predictable temp filenames can be pre-created or read across service boundaries, so a local foothold becomes cross-service interference; MEDIUM severity because it needs local access.

systemd:nonewprivs.recordDesc: NoNewPrivileges=no lets the service gain privileges at exec time through setuid binaries or file capabilities.
systemd:nonewprivs.risk: A compromised service escalates from its own account to root inside the unit; MEDIUM.

systemd:protectsys.recordDesc: ProtectSystem=no leaves /usr, /boot and /etc writable by the unit, instead of the read-only view that ProtectSystem=strict mounts.
systemd:protectsys.risk: A compromised service rewrites binaries, units or configuration that survive a restart; MEDIUM.

logrotate:mode.recordDesc: The create mode is group- or world-writable, so a rotated log file can be written by users other than its owner.
logrotate:mode.risk: A local user injects lines into logs that audits and alerts later trust; MEDIUM.

rsyslog:imtcp.recordDesc: $ModLoad imtcp opens a syslog listener that accepts plain TCP connections, so records travel without a TLS wrapper or a peer check.
rsyslog:imtcp.risk: Anyone on the network path reads, injects or replays log records; MEDIUM.

postfix:mynetworks.recordDesc: mynetworks = 0.0.0.0/0 tells Postfix that every address on the internet is a trusted relay client, so it skips the relay restrictions applied to unknown senders.
postfix:mynetworks.risk: The server relays mail for strangers, which spends the domain's reputation on spam; MEDIUM.

haproxy:stats.recordDesc: The stats socket on disk serves the runtime table, and an admin-level caller can change server state.
haproxy:stats.risk: A local user who can reach the socket reads traffic counters and drains or reconfigures backends; MEDIUM because it needs a foothold on the host.

squid:all.recordDesc: http_access allow all grants every request before any ACL is evaluated, and no deny rule follows it to close the proxy.
squid:all.risk: The proxy forwards anyone who can reach it, which hides their traffic behind the organisation's address; MEDIUM.

traefik:skipverify.recordDesc: insecureSkipVerify = true makes the proxy accept any certificate the backend presents.
traefik:skipverify.risk: A machine on the backend path impersonates the service and reads the proxied traffic; MEDIUM.

supervisor:chmod.recordDesc: The supervisor socket is created with a mode that lets other local users connect.
supervisor:chmod.risk: A local user starts, stops or reconfigures supervised programs, which is code execution as the supervisor account; MEDIUM.

gitlab:runnerpriv.recordDesc: privileged = true gives build containers the host's kernel capabilities and device access.
gitlab:runnerpriv.risk: A job from any project on that runner mounts the host filesystem and takes the runner host; MEDIUM.

title: Observability service left open ({fw}) — review required
description: {fw} runs with an open setting: {sink}. Default credentials and disabled auth expose metrics and data. This lexical rule flags the setting; the reviewer hardens via {safe}.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: matches the setting regardless of network scope.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on open settings ({fw}).
fp: Loopback-only instances are the common accepted case.
recordDesc: For {fw}, {sink} leaves the service open. The remedy is {safe}.
verifyT: Rescan shows no open setting reachable.

title: Wildcard IAM in {fw} — review required

limitation: Lexical, line-based: matches the wildcard regardless of trust policy.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on wildcard IAM ({fw}).
fp: Break-glass roles are the rare accepted case — confirm controls.
recordDesc: In {fw}, {sink} grants star permissions. The remedy is {safe}.
risk: Account compromise via the role; HIGH severity.

title: Public storage canned ACL ({fw}) — review required
description: {fw} sets a public canned ACL: {sink}. Objects become world-readable. This lexical rule flags the ACL; the reviewer confirms public intent or restricts via {safe}.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: matches the ACL regardless of bucket purpose.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on public ACLs ({fw}).

verifyT: Rescan shows no public ACL outside asset buckets.

cweDef.name: Inclusion of Functionality from Untrusted Control Sphere
cweDef.summary: Remote file inclusion executes code fetched from a URL as if it were local.

title: Remote file inclusion enabled (php) — review required

limitation: Lexical, line-based: matches the switch.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on the php.ini switch.
fp: None common — this switch is rarely justified.
recordDesc: With {sink}, include and require fetch URLs. The remedy is {safe}.
why: PHP includes remote URLs as code ({sink}).

title: PHP version exposure (php) — review required

limitation: Lexical, line-based: matches the switch.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on the php.ini switch.
fp: None common.
recordDesc: With {sink}, responses carry the PHP version. The remedy is {safe}.

remediation: Set {safe} or exclude sensitive files with backup rules.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: matches the flag.

fp: Local-only endpoints are the common accepted case.

cweDef.name: Improper Export of Android Application Components
cweDef.summary: Exported components accept intents from any app, exposing their actions to attackers.

title: Android component exported ({lang}) — review required
description: A component is exported: {sink}. Any app can invoke it. This lexical rule flags the flag; the reviewer confirms permission guards via {safe}.
remediation: Set exported false or guard with {safe}.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: matches the flag regardless of permissions.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on the manifest flag.
fp: Launcher activities are the common accepted case.
recordDesc: With {sink}, the component answers foreign intents. The remedy is {safe}.

title: Flask session cookie without Secure ({lang}) — review required
description: Flask session cookies may travel over HTTP: {sink}. Network observers steal the session. This lexical rule flags the setting; the reviewer enables {safe}.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: matches the setting.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on the Flask setting.
fp: Local development is the common false positive.
recordDesc: With {sink}, Flask sessions lack the Secure flag. The remedy is {safe}.

title: Rails force_ssl disabled ({lang}) — review required
description: Rails HTTPS enforcement is off: {sink}. Cookies and pages travel over HTTP. This lexical rule flags the setting; the reviewer enables {safe}.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: matches the setting.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on the Rails setting.
fp: Terminated-TLS frontends are the common accepted case — confirm headers.
recordDesc: With {sink}, Rails skips HTTPS redirect and secure cookies. The remedy is {safe}.
risk: Downgrade and cookie theft; MEDIUM severity.

title: Spring CSRF disabled ({lang}) — review required
description: Spring CSRF protection is disabled: {sink}. State-changing endpoints accept forged requests. This lexical rule flags the call; the reviewer restores {safe}.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: matches the call.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on the Spring call.
fp: Stateless token APIs are the common false positive.
recordDesc: With {sink}, Spring skips CSRF tokens. The remedy is {safe}.
applicability: Spring Security config; single-line lexical scope.

title: Debug or management exposure ({fw}) — review required
description: {fw} exposes introspection or management: {sink}. Introspection leaks schema; open actuators leak health, config, and dumps. This lexical rule flags the exposure; the reviewer restricts via {safe}.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: matches the exposure.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on exposure settings ({fw}).
fp: Internal-only services are the common accepted case.
recordDesc: With {sink}, {fw} exposes internals. The remedy is {safe}.
risk: Reconnaissance and data leaks; MEDIUM severity.

title: BinaryFormatter instantiation ({lang}) — review required
description: Code instantiates BinaryFormatter: {sink}. Its deserialization executes gadget chains on hostile bytes. This lexical rule flags the instantiation; the reviewer migrates to {safe}.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: matches instantiation.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on BinaryFormatter use in {lang} code.
fp: Trusted local state is the common false positive.
recordDesc: With {sink}, .NET deserializes object graphs. The remedy is {safe}.
verifyT: Rescan shows no BinaryFormatter on untrusted bytes.

title: Berkeley r-command use ({lang}) — review required
description: Code or scripts use rsh/rlogin: {sink}. Trust-based, cleartext remote execution. This lexical rule flags the use; the reviewer migrates to {safe}.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: matches the command name.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on r-command use.
fp: None common.
recordDesc: With {sink}, remote execution relies on host trust files and travels without encryption, so anyone on the path can read or alter the session. The remedy is SSH with per-user keys ({safe}).
risk: Credential theft and spoofing; MEDIUM severity.

title: OAuth implicit flow ({lang}) — review required
description: An OAuth request uses the implicit flow: {sink}. Tokens travel in URLs and fragments, leaking through history and referrers. This lexical rule flags the flow; the reviewer migrates to {safe}.
limitation: Lexical, line-based: matches the response type.
scopeT: Single-line lexical match on OAuth response types.
fp: None common.
recordDesc: With {sink}, tokens pass through the browser address bar. The remedy is {safe}.
why: OAuth implicit flow puts tokens in URLs ({sink}).
